A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEGADance work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The scientific content aligns throughout; v3 removes the trailing NeurIPS checklist and changes first-page metadata.

before.justification: v1 reports original FineDance and AIST++ evaluations, a user study, genre-control experiments and component ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–4 and the qualitative ablations in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The FSQ-based dance quantization, reconstruction losses, specialized and universal experts, Mamba-Transformer backbone and inference procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineDance, AIST++, the same in-the-wild music user study and the same genre-mismatch scenarios. No dataset, task or evaluated population is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Bailando++, FineNet and Lodge in Table 1; FACT, Bailando++, EDGE and Lodge in Table 2; and FineNet and Lodge in Table 3. The qualitative comparisons also retain the same methods.

E3.justification: Both retain 20 FineDance test clips with 1024-frame outputs, 40 AIST++ clips with 1200-frame outputs, and the 30-participant, five-point user study. Metrics, genre-control procedures, training settings and questionnaire controls are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same expert, Mamba, quantization and reconstruction-loss ablations. The genre-control examples and Appendix A.2 qualitative ablation analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3 removes checklist item 7's acknowledgment of this absence, but the statistical reporting practices for the results remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the qualitative findings are retained. For example, FineDance FIDk remains 50.00, AIST++ FIDk remains 25.89, and genre accuracy remains 75.64; no results are added or removed.

T1.justification: The problem definitions and Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Removing the checklist's generic assertion about complete proofs does not remove any mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about the first MoE architecture for music-to-dance generation, FSQ utilization, the hybrid backbone, state-of-the-art performance and genre controllability.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Appendix A.4's limitations concerning rigid genre labels, noisy motion data and overfitting remain unchanged. However, deleting the checklist removes the explicit acknowledgment that quantitative and user-study results lack uncertainty estimates and statistical tests.

D1.justification: Implementation and user-study details in Appendices A.1 and A.3 remain unchanged. Removing checklist item 5 deletes the assertion that code is available, while both abstracts promise release upon acceptance. This changes the availability disclosure without establishing an actual withdrawal of code.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, 45 bibliography entries and novelty positioning are unchanged. The revised publication-status footer does not change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 removes the trailing NeurIPS checklist and updates author-affiliation labels and publication-status wording. The scientific narrative, section order and Appendices A.1–A.4 otherwise remain unchanged; there is no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The first-page affiliation block and footer are adjusted, including replacement of the NeurIPS 2025 line with 'Preprint. Under review.' Figures 1–6, Tables 1–4, their captions and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the method, experimental evidence, scientific discussion and technical appendices. Clearer affiliation mapping and removal of the contradictory code-availability assertion provide small benefits, while the explicit statistical caveat disappears with the checklist. These limited disclosure and presentation edits do not materially change the paper's overall scientific support or reproducibility.
